subject: POC traffic burst signature + acceptance sprint plan
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC traffic burst signature + acceptance sprint plan

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get the POC scheduled and scoped: 

1) Workload profile we need from you (please prioritize):
   - Baseline sustained RPS: what does your normal production look like by endpoint (e.g., /generate, /embed)?
   - Burst profile: peak RPS during campaigns (99th / max), and typical burst duration (seconds/minutes).
   - Concurrency: number of simultaneous users/sessions hitting the same model instance.
   - Tokens per request: median, 75p, 95p for both input and output; typical prompt scaffolding size.
   - Payload mix: percent of short (<=64 tokens), medium (65–512), long (>512) requests.
   - Failure patterns: any downstream timeouts, retries, or 3rd-party latencies that affect request timing.

2) Success criteria (proposal):
   - Functional: 95% of requests must return a syntactically valid response per your schema.
   - Performance: p95 latency for /generate under POC target load <= 800ms (we can adjust once we see real token distributions).
   - Reliability: error rate < 1% for the measured windows (excluding bot traffic).
   - Cost sanity check: baseline per-1M-token cost estimate +/- 20% vs. target.

3) POC cadence & plan:
   - Probe week (we run a 48–72 hour throughput probe): Redwood SE (Ben) runs bench, you provide sample payloads + optional recorded traffic snapshot.
   - Acceptance sprint (2 weeks): run production-like traffic slices, validate metrics and run acceptance tests.
   - Roll/Cancel decision at sprint end based on throughput, latency, and quality guardrails.

4) Owners & asks:
   - BrightCart: Alex — provide payload samples, traffic snapshot, schema, and any auth/test tokens.
   - Redwood: Naomi (AM) — commercial / scheduling; Ben (SE) — probe & bench owner; Karthik — model/quantization recommendations and SLO target owner.

5) Deliverables before probe:
   - brightcart_sample_payloads.jsonl (10k lines representative)
   - traffic_snapshot_may2027.csv (1–7 day sample with timestamps and endpoint labels)
   - Signed mutual action plan doc (we'll share a template)

Target dates: can we get the sample payloads by EOD Tue (2027-05-11)? If yes we can start the probe during the week of 2027-05-17.

Thanks — I can pull a short MAP and a checklist after we get the samples.

— Naomi

Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC traffic burst signature + acceptance sprint plan

Thanks Naomi — solid recap. Apologies for the slightly delayed reply, pulled answers below and attached a small sample set.

Quick answers:
- Baseline sustained RPS: 12 RPS for /generate during business hours (PST) across NA region.
- Burst profile: up to 420 RPS for /generate during promotional pushes (~3–7 minutes), typical shock spikes at end of the hour.
- Concurrency: we see up to ~250 concurrent sessions hitting the same model during peaks.
- Tokens per request: median input 80 tokens, output median 120 tokens; 75p input 240, 95p input 760.
- Payload mix: ~55% short, 35% medium, 10% long.
- Retries: client library retries at 2xx->5xx for 500ms backoff; we'll strip retries for probe to measure raw service.

Attached: brightcart_sample_payloads.jsonl (1,500 lines, sampled), traffic_snapshot_may2027.csv (48h sample). Also shared a short MAP (mutual_action_plan_brightcart.docx) — filled the timeline preliminaries.

We accept the proposed success criteria, but would ask p95 latency target be flexible by +/-200ms depending on token mix; let's iterate after the probe.

Next steps: we'll get the signed MAP back by Thu 2027-05-13 and upload a larger 10k sample if probe start confirmed.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightCart
alex.johnson@brightcart.com

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC traffic burst signature + acceptance sprint plan

Great — appreciate the payloads. I'll call out how we'll run the probe and what we need to validate: 

Probe mechanics (what Redwood will do):
- Run a parameterized load run that mirrors your 48h sample at three scales: baseline, 2x, and peak. Peak scale will emulate the 420 RPS shock profile with the 3–7 minute burst windows.
- Token accounting: we will measure median/95p tokenization on Redwood side (we may observe small differences due to tokenization rules; we'll report both).
- KV cache behavior: if you use prompt-prefix caching, tell us which endpoints are eligible — that materially impacts per-token cost.

Acceptance checks we'll report:
- p95 latency per endpoint and token-length bucket
- 5-minute error rate and a timeline of any 5xx spikes
- Throughput plateau: can the baseline sustain continuous load for 60 minutes without degradation
- Cost estimate: per-1M-token extrapolation for observed mix

Open asks from BrightCart for the probe:
- Confirm whether the sample payloads include auth headers or if we should use a test key (preferred).
- Tell us which endpoint we should prioritize if we can't run both /generate + /rerank in the first probe.

I'll create a short runbook with commands and a shared dashboard (Grafana link) — will post the link in HubSpot and in this thread.

Ben

Subject: Re: POC traffic burst signature + acceptance sprint plan

Quick alignment from my side: we can support the 420 RPS burst shape but will recommend a probe configuration that isolates latency sources (model vs infra). Proposed short checklist: 
- Redwood will run model-variant A (float16) and a quantized variant if BrightCart is comfortable; we will compare p95/p99.
- Please confirm a list of 5 golden queries (small set) for functional validation across the long/short mixes.
- We'll tag results to the MAP and produce a one-page readout for your ops team.

If BrightCart signs the MAP by Thu (2027-05-13) we'll target a probe kickoff on Mon (2027-05-17). Ben, I'll coordinate the variant matrix and post the notes to the shared Drive.

— Karthik
